title: Learning mechanical systems from real-world data using discrete forced Lagrangian dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2505.20370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We introduce a data-driven method for learning the equations of motion of mechanical systems directly from position measurements. This is particularly relevant in system identification tasks where only positional information is available, such as motion capture, pixel data or low-resolution tracking. Our approach takes advantage of the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the forced discrete Euler-Lagrange equations to construct a physically grounded model of the system's dynamics. We decompose the dynamics into conservative and non-conservative components, which are learned separately using feed-forward neural networks. In the absence of external forces, our method reduces to a variational discretization of the action principle naturally preserving the symplectic structure of the underlying Hamiltonian system. translated_title: 基于离散受迫拉格朗日动力学从真实世界数据中学习机械系统
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种数据驱动方法，可直接从位置测量数据中学习机械系统的运动方程。这在仅有位置信息可用的系统辨识任务中尤为重要，例如动作捕捉、像素数据或低分辨率跟踪场景。我们的方法利用离散拉格朗日-达朗贝尔原理和受迫离散欧拉-拉格朗日方程来构建具有物理基础的动力系统模型。我们将动力学分解为保守分量与非保守分量，并使用前馈神经网络分别进行学习。在没有外力的情况下，我们的方法可归结为作用量原理的变分离散化，从而自然地保持底层哈密顿系统的辛结构。我们在多种合成数据集和真实世界数据集上验证了该方法，展示了其有效性。
tldr: 该论文提出一种基于离散拉格朗日-达朗贝尔原理的数据驱动方法，仅利用位置测量数据即可学习机械系统的运动方程，通过神经网络分别学习保守与非保守动力学分量，并能自然保持系统的辛结构。
